newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit eases, market awaits intervention.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit eases, market awaits intervention.

text.p: Ringgit eased under sustained selling by U.S. banks overseas as the market waited for Bank Negara's agents to intervene around 2.6350 to a dollar level, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said some prominent Asian banks had been roped in by the Malaysian central bank to carry out its operation.
At 0820 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6335/65 to a dollar, rising from a morning low of 2.6230.
"We are waiting to see if some Asian bank will come in now. They were in in the morning at 2.6350/70 level," a dealer with a European bank in Singapore said.
Dealers said one Kuala Lumpur-based foreign bank came in briefly around 0825 GMT, purportedly on behalf of the central bank, but no confirmation was available.
Bank Negara does not comment on its open market operations.
"We are not sure if there is any intervention at all. The said banks could be taking their own positions," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur.
Dealers said the pressure on ringgit was expected to continue in the near-term.
"Most people seem to be expecting a downside for ringgit," said a Singapore-based currency analyst.
